samples.summary: replacePrefixes lets the selection map by default, so a caret at column 0 ends up BEFORE the inserted list marker
samples.evidence: `replacePrefixes` dispatches `state.update({ changes, userEvent: 'input' })` with no `selection`. CodeMirror maps the selection with assoc -1, so a cursor sitting exactly at `line.from` (the change's `from`) stays at `line.from`, i.e. in front of the `- ` / `1. ` / `- [ ] ` just written. The very same hazard is called out and fixed in the pre-existing sibling command: commands.ts:301-309 `toggleQuote` deliberately does `selection: state.selection.map(changeSet, 1)` with the comment "a caret sitting exactly at a line start would otherwise stay *before* the `> ` just inserted there, so the next keystroke would land ahead of the marker". The new code repeats the bug the old code documents. Reachable on the common paths: toggling a list on an empty line (list-commands.test.ts:96 `mount('', 0)` — the test only asserts the doc text, never the caret) or with the caret at the start of a line. The next typed character lands before the bullet and destroys the list item.

samples.summary: Early returns in onTaskClick run after the browser already flipped the checkbox, without preventDefault — preview shows a checked state the source does not have
samples.evidence: `onTaskClick` returns early for `e.detail > 1` (line 271), for a nested `li` (line 282) and for `selectionTouches(item)` (line 286). All of these returns happen *before* `e.preventDefault()` (line 303). When the click landed on the `<input type="checkbox">` itself, the browser has already toggled the DOM `checked` state, and cancelling is the only thing that reverts it. On the `detail > 1` path (a user double-clicking a checkbox to tick then untick — well within the double-click interval, same position, so the second click carries `detail: 2`) the second click is ignored, nothing is written to the document, and no re-render occurs (renderPreview only runs on `docChanged`, editor.ts:421). The preview is then left displaying the opposite of what the note says, indefinitely. Fix: either `preventDefault()` before the guards when the target is the checkbox, or force a re-render.

samples.summary: selectionTouches' `container.contains(item)` branch makes any selection elsewhere on the page suppress task toggling
samples.evidence: `if (item.contains(container) || container.contains(item)) return true;` — `commonAncestorContainer` for a selection spanning two unrelated paragraphs is a shared ancestor (the preview root, or `<body>`), which `contains(item)` for every task item in the document, not just the one being clicked. The guard therefore reports "the user is selecting this item" for a selection anywhere in the page whose common ancestor happens to enclose the item. This is mostly masked because mousedown collapses the document selection, but clicking a form control (the checkbox) does not reliably clear an existing selection in every browser, in which case a task click is silently dropped with no feedback. Narrowing to "the range intersects the item" (e.g. `range.intersectsNode(item)`) would be correct.

samples.summary: computeActiveFormats now parses every selected line on every selection/doc change — O(selected lines) per keystroke
samples.evidence: `computeActiveFormats` unconditionally calls `computeListState(state)` (commands.ts:64), which calls `selectedTargets` → `selectedLines`, building a `ParsedLine` (regex exec per line) for *every* line the main selection covers (list-commands.ts:89-101). editor.ts:420-425 invokes `computeActiveFormats` on `u.docChanged || u.selectionSet`, i.e. on every keystroke and every caret move. With a select-all in a large note (or typing while a large block is selected) this becomes a full-document regex pass per event, on the UI thread. The previous inline-format computation was O(1) around the caret. A cheap bound (e.g. cap the scanned lines, or only inspect the first/last lines plus a limit) would keep the toolbar honest without the scan.

samples.summary: A checkbox with no text after it (`- [ ] ` / `- [ ]`) is a task to the editor but not to the preview, so it renders as a plain bullet and cannot be clicked
samples.evidence: `toggleTaskList` on an empty line produces exactly `- [ ] ` (asserted at list-commands.test.ts:96-99), and `LIST_RE` (line 32) classifies it as a task. markdown-it-task-lists only converts an item whose inline content starts with `'[ ] '` (a trailing space after the box, and markdown-it trims the item's trailing whitespace), so `- [ ] ` with empty content renders as an ordinary bullet with a literal `[ ]`, not as a checkbox. Result: after pressing the new Checkbox toolbar button on an empty line, the toolbar shows the Checkbox toggle pressed while the preview shows no checkbox until the user types text. Same mismatch for `setTaskChecked`, which will happily consider such a line a task.
searchedFor: markdown-it-task-lists source (not installed in the working tree; reasoned from the published v2 implementation)

samples.summary: The pointer cursor covers the whole task `li`, including nested non-task children that the click handler deliberately ignores
samples.evidence: .note-preview.note-tasks-interactive li.task-list-item { cursor: pointer } applies to the entire subtree area of a task item, but `onTaskClick` bails out for any click whose `target.closest('li')` is a nested item (preview.ts:281-282, covered by the 'leaves a plain nested item under a task to that item' test). A nested plain bullet under a task therefore shows a pointer cursor and does nothing when clicked — the affordance contradicts the behaviour. The rule should target the item's own content (or exclude descendants of nested `li`s).

samples.summary: List commands dispatch without scrollIntoView, unlike the analogous toggleQuote
samples.evidence: `replacePrefixes` (line 208) omits `scrollIntoView: true`, which commands.ts:311 sets for the equivalent line-prefix command. When the toolbar action is applied to a selection that has been scrolled out of view (the toolbar has focus, not the editor), the edited block is not brought back into view.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repository: `replacePrefixes` (list-commands.ts:207-209) dispatches `state.update({ changes, userEvent: 'input' })` with no `selection`, so the selection maps with CodeMirror's default assoc -1. For a line with no marker, the change is a pure insertion at `p.line.from` (to = line.to - content.length == line.from, lines 200-201), so a caret at column 0 stays before the inserted `- ` / `1. ` / `- [ ] `; the next keystroke lands ahead of the marker and breaks the list item. The identical hazard is explicitly handled in the sibling command commands.ts:301-309 (`toggleQuote` uses `state.selection.map(changeSet, 1)` with a comment describing exactly this failure), confirming the semantics and that the new code omits the fix. No transactionFilter/selection fix-up exists anywhere in packages/notes/src (grep found only commands.ts:309). The path is reachable from the toolbar via editor.ts:581-585 and notes-toolbar.tsx:303, and is exercised in list-commands.test.ts:101-106 (`mount('', 0)`), which asserts only doc text and never the caret; the existing caret test (lines 49-55) uses a caret mid-content so it does not cover column 0. Real, unguarded, reachable incorrect-state bug in the correctness lane.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repository: onTaskClick returns early at preview.ts:271 (e.detail > 1), :282 (nested li) and :286 (selectionTouches) — all before e.preventDefault() at :303. The repo's own comment (preview.ts:297-299) and test ('cancels the click it turns into a toggle', preview.test.ts:125-138) confirm the browser has already flipped the checkbox's `checked` before the click handler runs and that cancelling is the only revert. On the detail>1 path (an ordinary double-click on the checkbox) nothing is dispatched, so no docChanged fires and renderPreview (editor.ts:421) never runs, leaving the preview showing the opposite of the source. It is also sticky: setTaskChecked returns without dispatching when the source already matches (list-commands.ts:294), so a later click reports the already-current state, produces no re-render, and preventDefault re-reverts the visual flip — the mismatch cannot be cleared by clicking. No guard, caller, or other listener elsewhere compensates (the only other preview listener is the copy-button handler at preview.ts:227; no change/mouseup handlers exist). Real, reachable, incorrect-state bug in the correctness lane.
